text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition FORD-Asili party Chairman Kenneth Matiba's rejection of the National Convention Executive Committee (NCEC) draws mixed reaction from the opposition demanding political reforms.
- Kenya's parliament will sit throughout August to finish urgent and mandatory business before the general election.
- Kenya's ambassador to the United States says Kenya will defend its political and human rights record before the U.S. Senate.
- An armed suspect and 15 remand prisoners escape from a police vehicle ferrying them back to custody.
- Several members of parliament from the ruling Kenya African National Union party and the opposition launch a lobby group to mediate between the government and opposition.
- The NCEC holds a crisis meeting to discuss Matiba's stand on constitutional reforms and resolve to accommodate his views.
- The government acknowledges receiving proposals on constitutional reforms from the NCEC.
- The speaker of the national assembly warns members of parliament against importing "hooligans" to disrupt business in the house.
- Fourteen clergymen from the Anglican Church of the Province of Kenya are to quit and join the Episcopal Church of Africa. ($1=58 Kenyan Shillings)
